## Vision

Audience Score System helps a YouTube creator and their analyst turn a hunch into a greenlit, published video, and then tells them whether they were right. It closes three coupled loops — research a topic into a grounded viability call, turn viable ideas into video scripts the creator greenlights, and check the published outcome against what was predicted — so that judgment about "what will work" gets calibrated by real outcomes over time instead of staying confident guesswork. The product itself holds no opinion: it is a Postgres-backed research/script/outcome store wrapping the YouTube Data and Analytics APIs, exposed over MCP so any MCP-capable agent (Claude, Copilot, opencode, Antigravity, etc.) can do the reasoning while the system makes that reasoning durable, cited, and checkable against reality.

## Personas

- **Creator** — Owns Channels and holds final decision authority: only a Creator on a Channel can approve a video script or turn a viability verdict into a commitment. Drives research closely alongside the Analyst in V1.
- **Analyst** — Does research and builds proposed plans/video scripts for the Creator's review; no approve/finalize authority on any Channel. Work is mutually visible with the Creator's.

## Load-bearing decisions

### LB1 — YouTube OAuth consent scope requested at signup

At risk: C9 (CTR/impressions metrics) and C16 (deeper Analytics: retention curves, traffic sources, subscriber conversion).

Decide now: request the full YouTube Analytics **owner-level** scope (`yt-analytics.readonly` + `yt-analytics-monetary.readonly` if any monetary-adjacent field is ever wanted, otherwise just the owner-level non-monetary scope — confirm which C16 fields need) at every Creator's initial OAuth consent in M1, even though V1 only stores/surfaces views + retention + CTR/impressions. Re-consent is a re-auth flow through Google's consent screen for every already-connected Creator — cheap for a handful of dogfood users now, a real support/adoption cost once C11 (multi-Channel) and C12 exist and there are many connected accounts.

Stays cheap: which Analytics *fields* get queried, cached, and surfaced (traffic sources, subscriber conversion, retention curves) — that's application-layer scope entirely inside the sync job and read models, addable without touching the OAuth grant at all once the scope is already held.

### LB2 — Persona↔Channel association schema, asymmetric authority

At risk: C12 (Analyst across multiple Channels) and C13 (multiple Creators per Channel).

Decide now: model Persona↔Channel as a join table from day one (`channel_id`, `person_id`, `role` ∈ {creator, analyst}, plus invite/accept state), with authorization checks (`can_approve`, `can_invite`) reading the role off that table rather than off a single `channel.owner_id` column or an assumption of "the one Creator" baked into video-script/verdict approval logic. M1 only ever populates one row of each role per Channel, but every approve/finalize check must already ask "is this person a Creator *on this Channel*" via the join, not via a hardcoded single-owner field.

Stays cheap: the invite UI/flow itself, multi-Creator conflict resolution (what happens when two Creators disagree — not specified anywhere, rightly deferred), and the Analyst-works-across-Channels list view — all additive once the join table and role-scoped authority checks already exist.

### LB4 — MCP write-back tool idempotency and statelessness

Protects the narrowed non-goal "ASS does not host its own agent loop — it embeds whagent-net's" (amendment `whagent-net-embed`, issue #1562) — not a numbered capability, but a permanent architectural constraint. An embedded whagent-net session calling `save_research_note`/`save_viability_verdict`/`save_video_script` is exactly the kind of MCP client this LB protects against — retried without call-to-call process affinity.

Decide now: every write-back tool (`save_research_note`, `save_viability_verdict`, `save_video_script`) must be safely re-callable with the same logical input (client-supplied idempotency key, or natural-key upsert) and must not assume any server-side state survives between tool calls beyond what's in Postgres — no in-memory session, no assumption that the calling agent process is the same process across calls. MCP clients (Claude, Copilot, opencode, Antigravity) retry tool calls on ambiguous failures and don't guarantee call-to-call process affinity; a V1 shortcut that works today because one agent session happens to hold state in its own context is exactly the kind of thing that gets threaded through every tool handler and is expensive to unpick once several write-back tools exist and clients are already depending on the current (accidentally stateful) behavior.

Stays cheap: adding more write-back tools, adding more read tools, changing what a tool returns — none of that touches the idempotency contract once every tool already treats Postgres as the only state.

### LB6 — ASS web takes a RabbitMQ dependency to live-follow an embedded whagent-net session

At risk: C21 (embedded research agent in ASS `web`) and the narrowed non-goal's "embeds whagent-net's" half — an embedded session a Creator/Analyst can't watch update live is not actually embedded, it's a black box with a submit button.

Decide now: ASS `web` takes a direct RabbitMQ dependency so it can run its own `htmxsse.Hub` bound to `whagent_net/events`, mirroring whagent-net's own M2 standalone-UI wiring (`whagent_net/product/03-roadmap.md`'s M2 design-time note: "the UI binds `htmxsse.Hub` to `whagent_net/events` directly") — rather than fronting the exchange through `api.StreamEvents`, whagent-net's credential-free path for clients that don't hold RMQ access (its C17). Live-following an embedded session is C21's core behavior, not an optional enhancement: a save-and-poll UI over the session record is not what "run a research agent inside ASS's web UI" describes. Confirm at C21's design time whether ASS already holds RMQ credentials for another consumer that this can reuse, or whether this is a net-new credential to provision. (As of 2026-10-01 ASS has no RabbitMQ dependency; the decision is not yet exercised.)

Stays cheap: which pages embed the session component, any session-list/history view over it, and ASS-specific chrome around the embedded session — all additive once the Hub is wired to the bus.

### LB3 — Prediction-vs-outcome record shape

At risk: C10 (browsing past comparisons) and C14 (calibration trends across many ideas).

Amended by `video-script-model` (issue #1562): the chain changed from `idea → verdict → schedule_draft → committed_schedule_entry → published_video_metrics` to `idea → verdict → video_script → published_video_metrics`, with `video_script` also carrying a `strategy_id` for grouping/cadence context only — not part of the identity path.

Decide now: `video_script` carries its own direct `verdict_id` FK (and `idea_id` transitively through the verdict) — mirroring what `schedule_entry` did before it was dropped — so the chain from idea to published outcome has a stable, non-lossy identity path that does not route through Strategy. `strategy_id` on `video_script` is grouping/cadence context only, never the identity path: Strategy is many-to-many with verdicts (`store/strategy.go`'s `SaveStrategyInput.VerdictIDs []uuid.UUID`; the doc comment is explicit that "the same verdict may be passed to more than one Strategy"), so if a `video_script`'s identity were resolved via `strategy_id` alone, a Strategy grouping 5 viable verdicts would yield 5 candidate verdicts per video_script — not one. That is precisely the identity-loss failure this LB exists to prevent. C14's calibration-trend view is an aggregate query over the idea→verdict→video_script→outcome chain; if idea identity is lost or duplicated anywhere in it, that aggregate requires a backfill/reconciliation pass instead of a `GROUP BY`.

Stays cheap: the trend visualization itself, any cross-idea statistical aggregation (accuracy rate, confidence calibration curves) — all read-side, addable once the FK chain exists.

### LB5 — Web/MCP dual-surface parity mechanism

At risk: C4, C5, C9, C10, C14 (each became dual-surface as its own M4.x milestone shipped), and NFR3's web-minimization intent (`ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "NFR3 interface allocation" section).

Decide now: every M4.x web surface must call the identical store method and identical `store.CanX` authorization check its MCP-tool counterpart already uses — never a parallel or divergent write/read path. This is the same "two independent, equally-capable front ends onto the same store, not a primary and a read-only shadow" pattern `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s NFR3 amendment established for C8 (issue #1648) and C11/C12/C13 (issue #1728); M4 generalized it to the remaining MCP-only capabilities. C4/C5's web surface is scoped to save + browse only — the persisted note/verdict CRUD and its rendering, the same objects `save_research_note`/`save_viability_verdict` already write — never ASS's own chat/reasoning implementation: the research/viability reasoning conversation itself stays either an external MCP-capable agent's job, or (C21) an embedded whagent-net session's, per the narrowed non-goal (amendment `whagent-net-embed`, issue #1562) — never something C4/C5's own web surface implements in-process. Each M4.x milestone appends its own `**NFR3 amendment (issue #<root plan issue>): <capabilities> are dual-surface.**` paragraph to `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "NFR3 interface allocation" section (mirroring the #1648 and #1728 paragraphs: same heading shape, same "which store method / which `CanX` check" content) — a milestone is not done reallocating interface until its own paragraph exists. A browser save-form's retry model (double-submit on back-button/refresh) differs from LB4's original agent-tool-call-retry framing; the shared store method should inherit LB4's contract rather than needing its own — confirm, don't assume, in each milestone's design pass. The current allocation of web-only versus dual-surface capabilities lives in `architecture/05-nfr3-interface-allocation.md`.

Stays cheap: which pages exist, their layout/UX, and the M4.1/M4.2/M4.3 phase ordering itself — all additive once every write/read path is already routed through the shared store+authz layer.

## Non-goals

**Permanent:**

- **No platforms beyond YouTube.** No platforms beyond YouTube, ever.
- **ASS does not host its own agent loop — it embeds whagent-net's.** MCP plus an external MCP-capable client (or an embedded whagent-net session acting on a Creator/Analyst's behalf) remains the permanent architecture; ASS never builds or runs its own in-process agent reasoning loop. Narrowed by amendment `whagent-net-embed` (issue #1562) from the original "No hosted/in-product agent loop, ever".
- **No monetization or billing.** No monetization or billing on the roadmap.
- **No personas beyond Creator and Analyst.** No personas beyond Creator and Analyst.
